issues.what: Carchemish drawn as an Assyrian vassal from 870 to the end of the window; its dossier bridged the 870 vassal_start to 717. The page dates tribute only to Sangara (870-848) and says Carchemish does not appear in Assyrian sources again until the mid-8th century (one brief mention under Shamshi-Adad V).
Sam'al drawn as an Assyrian vassal from 825 to the end of the window; the dossier bridged to 717 although its page says Sam'al became independent after Shalmaneser III's death (824).
Kummuh drawn as Assyrian vassal -866 on: the page has it 'a peaceful tributary state allied with Assyria' from the 9th to the mid-8th century and the 805 appeal to Adad-nirari III.
Gurgum drawn as Assyrian vassal -858 on: tribute 858 and 853, and in 805 Adad-nirari III fixed the Gurgum-Kummuh border; a coalition against Zakkur c. 800 does not clearly end the tie.

Neo-Hittite states aggregate (31 cells) is tinted as Assyrian vassal from -868 only because the Carchemish tribute is used as an overlap device with Assyria's -800 shape; the page names Carchemish alone and the tribute ended 848. Left because ending it would change how the -800 keyframes overlap in m0800-m0701.

Six keyframe snaps at -900 (elam +129/-18, phrygia +31/-40, neo-assyrian-empire +56, 22nd dynasty -44 Aswan cells, israel +7/-2, judah -3): each lands on the Cliopatria shape the dossier accepts ('ok'); Phrygia's found circle around Gordion differs from the shape, the shape wins; the Aswan cells are Lower Nubia south of the cataract, left unowned.

15 size-rule conflicts, 126 cell-years, none over 33; in each the smaller, more specific state (bit-yakin, elam, bit-agusi, carchemish, kummuh, sam-al, ammon) wins over the larger general one (babylonia, neo-hittite-states, israel), which is right.

Contest of the 22nd and 23rd dynasties from -826 covers 560 cells, 469 of them in Al Wadi at Jadid (Western Desert); the Nile valley governorates are only about 30 cells. It follows the dossier's reading of Cliopatria's Upper Egypt shape and the whole-governorate convention used for Egypt; no page gives a narrower land.
Xianyun drawn as a 616-cell state (a Hetao strip plus Ningxia) although the dossier calls it a people with a range, not a border; only the Hetao-to-upper-Yellow-River sentence supports the extent.
Qedar appears in -853 with 417 cells (Al Jawf) from Gindibu at Qarqar; infobox says 9th century, the extent is the researcher's reading.
